name: Asylum / Refugee Status

requirements.blocker_text: Under the Refugees Act [Chapter 4:03], an applicant applies to an authorized officer (police or immigration), who forwards the application to the Commissioner for Refugees within 5 days. The Zimbabwean Refugees Committee must consider it within 30 days and advises the Commissioner, who then recognizes or refuses recognition; appeals go to the Minister, whose decision is final. Recognized refugees receive identity cards and the same wage-earning work rights and restrictions as other non-citizens (not special or unrestricted work access), plus rights to religion, property acquisition, courts, education, and housing. The Minister may designate specific areas where refugees must reside -- in practice, this is Tongogara Refugee Settlement.
requirements.fix_path: Apply to a police or immigration officer, who refers the case to the Commissioner for Refugees within 5 days.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: the Minister may designate a required residence area (encampment) -- Tongogara Refugee Settlement in current practice

sources.title: ILO NATLEX -- hosted text of Zimbabwe's Refugees Act [Chapter 4:03]: the Commissioner/Committee/Minister decision chain, 5-day and 30-day procedural timelines, rights granted, encampment-designation power, and Zimbabwe's party status to the 1951 Convention, 1967 Protocol, and 1969 OAU Convention (all incorporated via Schedule I)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Zimbabwe). STATUS: DRAFT despite tier-2 sourcing (ILO NATLEX hosts the primary legislative text, consistent with this dataset's convention for intergovernmental-hosted legal text, but this dataset's validator requires tier-1 government sourcing specifically to publish a hard requirement) -- a ZimLII or government-gazette copy of the same Act was not independently cross-checked in this build. REAL, FUNCTIONING SYSTEM WITH CLEAR PROCEDURAL TIMELINES: unusually specific deadlines (5 days to refer, 30 days for Committee review) and full party status to all three major refugee-law instruments (1951 Convention, 1967 Protocol, 1969 OAU Convention) place this closer to Kazakhstan/Montenegro/DR Congo's functioning systems built elsewhere in this dataset than to Kuwait/Lebanon/Syria's thin-or-absent frameworks. ENCAMPMENT POLICY, EXPLICITLY DISCLOSED: the Minister's power to designate a mandatory residence area is not merely theoretical -- Tongogara Refugee Settlement (established 1983) is Zimbabwe's long-standing designated site, and search results reviewed in this build reference an ongoing 'protection gap' in the settlement as of a 2026 policy article, though that article's specific findings were not independently fetched for this file. work_rights set 'restricted' reflecting the Act's own framing (refugees get the SAME restrictions as other non-citizens, not special access); family_can_work left null since the Act did not address dependents separately from the principal refugee.
